scope: 01–25: foundations, coding, multiuser channels, statistical inference, cross-entropy and deep learning, information bottleneck, and finite-sample information estimation; logarithms base 2 unless stated

claims.statement: I(x)=-log2 p(x); entropy is average surprisal
Bayes theorem and Jensen inequality require their stated probability and positivity assumptions
H(X)=-sum p log2 p; H(X,Y)=H(X)+H(Y|X)
I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y), DPI for X->Y->Z
claims.toy: BSC epsilon=0.1: I=1-h2(.1)

claims.statement: H(p,q)=H(p)+D(p||q), D>=0, not symmetric
Entropy for finite alphabets is concave and bounded above by log2 M; conditioning reduces entropy only on average; the discrete maximum entropy problem requires explicit constraints
claims.toy: X1 fair, X2=X1, X3 independent fair -> joint entropy=2 bits

claims.statement: For i.i.d. finite-alphabet sources -log2 P(X^n)/n converges in probability to entropy. Typical set high-probability and cardinality bounds are asymptotic.
claims.toy: Bernoulli(.25), n=8, epsilon=.15 -> mass=.31146240234375

claims.statement: For binary uniquely decodable source codes, H(X)<=L; Shannon prefix lengths ceil(-log2 p) achieve L<H+1; prefix lengths satisfy Kraft.
Huffman greedy merge produces minimum mean length among binary symbol-by-symbol prefix codes with known symbol weights.
Arithmetic encoding refines [L,U) using both new endpoints from old bounds, and exact dyadic inclusion allows a finite prefix; finite precision requires renormalization and termination protocol.
LZ77 copies from an already decoded sliding window and may overlap; LZ78 builds phrase indices; DEFLATE couples LZ77 matches and Huffman codes with a 32KiB history limit.
claims.toy: ABCABCABC -> literal A,B,C plus match(distance=3,length=6); LZ78 ABABABA -> A|B|AB|ABA

claims.statement: DMC channel kernels are conditional row-normalized matrices. BSC/BEC have distinct noise semantics and two independent BSCs cascade with epsilon=p+q-2pq.
claims.toy: BSC(.1) with uniform input I=.5310044; cascade BSC(.1),BSC(.2) => effective error .26

claims.statement: DMC capacity is max over input distributions, not mutual information at arbitrary prior; symmetric BSC/BEC admit closed forms and BA optimizes general finite channel capacity.

claims.statement: For stationary finite DMC, rate R<C admits a sequence of codes with vanishing average block error; weak converse via Fano and I(M;Y^n)≤nC forbids vanishing error for R>C.
claims.toy: BSC(.1) C≈.5310044; repetition n=3 p=.1: block error=.028 with rate=1/3

claims.statement: Hamming(7,4) with parity at positions 1,2,4 corrects one bit by s=Hr^T; 16 radius-one balls size 8 partition all 128 seven-bit vectors.

claims.statement: Cyclic codes are ideals in GF(2)[x]/(x^n−1). CRC systematic encoding appends the remainder of x^r M modulo G. An error is undetected iff G divides E; degree-r G with nonzero constant term detects every burst of length at most r. CRC-32/ISO-HDLC requires its full parameter tuple.
claims.toy: G=1011, message 1101 -> codeword 1101001, remainder 000; CRC32 check vector 123456789 -> CBF43926

claims.statement: A rate-1/2 K=3 (7,5)_8 convolutional encoder with state=(previous,older) has four states. Hard-decision Viterbi retains the minimum accumulated Hamming-metric path per state, with initial/final states and tail bits explicit.
claims.toy: message 1011 plus tail 00 -> 111000010111; one encoded bit flip is recovered

claims.statement: Perfect secrecy is I(M;C)=0 or posterior invariance. H(K)>=H(M) is necessary, not sufficient. OTP needs a uniform independent equal-length key used once. The degraded wiretap formula requires the stated DMC assumptions.
claims.toy: uniform M and Bernoulli(q) XOR key: I(M;C)=1-h2(q), zero only at q=.5

claims.statement: R(D) minimizes mutual information subject to expected distortion. Bernoulli Hamming and Gaussian squared-error sources have distinct closed forms; independent Gaussian vectors use reverse water-filling. JPEG quantization, not DCT alone, introduces primary irreversible loss.
claims.toy: Bernoulli(.2), D=.1 => .2529325 bit/symbol; Gaussian variance1,D=.25 => 1 bit/symbol; vector variances(1,4,9), D=4 => theta=1.5, R=2

claims.statement: Differential entropy transforms as h(aX+b)=h(X)+log2|a| for a!=0; Gaussian maximizes entropy at fixed covariance. Real scalar AWGN capacity is .5 log2(1+P/N0) bits/real use; independent parallel real subchannels use water-filling.

For the two-user real Gaussian MAC with independent Gaussian codebooks and average powers P1,P2 over noise variance N, the capacity region is R1≤1/2log2(1+P1/N), R2≤1/2log2(1+P2/N), R1+R2≤1/2log2(1+(P1+P2)/N). SIC decoding orders attain the two dominant-face corner points. For general relay DMCs, cut-set is an upper bound and decode-forward is an achievable lower bound; general relay capacity is not characterized by the cut-set bound. Network coding can improve multicast rates in the butterfly topology.

Under regularity conditions Fisher information is the variance of the score and local KL curvature; n iid samples add information. The scalar CRLB for an unbiased estimator of g(theta) is g'(theta)^2/(n J1(theta)). Standard CRLB fails for parameter-dependent support such as U(0,theta). AIC estimates asymptotic predictive KL risk; BIC is a regular-model Laplace approximation to marginal likelihood; MDL is a family of code-length principles.
claims.toy: N(mu,4), n=100 => Fisher information 25 and sample-mean variance/CRLB=.04; logL=-50,k=3,n=100 => AIC=106,BIC≈113.8155

claims.statement: For normalized target distribution y and softmax q, cross-entropy is H(y)+KL(y||q) and its logit gradient is q-y. Brier/squared probability error is also a proper scoring rule; CE is not universally superior. Label smoothing mixes one-hot targets with uniform mass. VAE ELBO combines expected reconstruction log likelihood with KL(q(z|x)||p(z)).
claims.toy: logits=(2,0,-1), target class 1 => p1≈.1142, CE≈2.1698, target-logit gradient≈−.8858; binary Brier logit gradient is 2(q−y)q(1−q)

claims.statement: The classical IB objective minimizes I(X;T)-beta I(T;Y) under T-X-Y. Under this Markov condition, expected KL task distortion E D_KL(p(y|x)||p(y|t)) equals I(X;Y)-I(T;Y). VIB upper-bounds I(X;T) with E KL(q(t|x)||r(t)) and optimizes a predictive likelihood lower bound. Information-plane compression is not universal; deterministic continuous representations can have divergent mutual information.
claims.toy: Illustrative Pareto points (I(X;T),I(T;Y))={(0,0),(.5,.35),(1,.62),(1.5,.78),(2,.86),(2.5,.90)}; β selects argmin IXT−βITY

claims.statement: Finite-sample plug-in entropy is typically downward biased for fixed finite support; Miller–Madow is a first-order correction. KSG-1 estimates continuous MI from joint max-norm k-neighbor radii and marginal counts, yielding nats before conversion to bits. MINE is a neural DV variational lower bound; InfoNCE is a contrastive MI lower bound capped by log K nats. Neither neural objective is an unbiased finite-sample MI measurement.
claims.toy: Bivariate Gaussian rho=.7 => I=−.5log2(1−.7²)≈.485 bit; InfoNCE with K candidates has upper bound log K nats
